title: Tetris' 'kill screen' wasn't the end after all
description: NES Tetris was thought unbeatable past level 29. Players broke that, and in 2023 a teenager crashed the game.

scenes.say: For years, NES Tetris was considered impossible past level twenty nine. Then players kept proving that wrong.
In 2011, Thor Aackerlund showed level twenty nine could be beaten. Joseph Saelee reached level thirty one in 2018, and hypertappers hit thirty eight by 2020.
On level twenty nine, pieces fall one row every frame. That's too fast for almost everyone, so for years it looked like a hard wall.

scenes.caption: Rolling, not tapping
scenes.say: A technique called rolling, developed in 2020, let players survive that speed. On December twenty first, 2023, thirteen year old Willis Gibson played past level one forty eight, and the game crashed at level one fifty seven.
That crash is popularly counted as beating Tetris, since the game can't truly be won. Follow for more record breakers and gaming history.
